evidence: New in this delta, from reading fix round 3 with the deletion-first eye. src/pool.ts:1129 now lists worktrees with `git worktree list --porcelain -z`. `-z` on `worktree list` is not in every git this kernel can meet (git added it in 2.36; Ubuntu 22.04's apt git is 2.34.1, Debian 11's is 2.30), and the kernel declares no git floor: src/commands/doctor.ts:216 checkGit reports PASS for any version that answers `--version`, and `grep -rniE 'git (version )?(>=|2\.[0-9]+)|minimum git|GIT_MIN' src README.md package.json` finds no requirement. When the listing exits nonzero, src/pool.ts:1130 `if (listed.status === 0)` skips the whole foreign-worktree read, `branchCheckedOutAt` stays undefined, the stage-2 refusal at src/pool.ts:1203 does not fire, and stage 3 deletes the branch with `update-ref -d` (src/pool.ts:1294), which src/pool.ts:1208 itself says does not check worktrees. Nothing records that the listing failed.

MEASURED at ea3edb3, node v26.6.0, dist/ built, by the CLI on a hand-built fleet (tiphys init, an upstream with one commit cloned to projects/demo, `pool create --task t-old`, then `git worktree add --force <tmp>/foreign task/t-old`, so a FOREIGN worktree holds the task branch), same fixture twice, one variable changed, a `git` wrapper first on PATH that rejects exactly `worktree list ... -z` with `error: unknown switch 'z'` exit 129 and execs /usr/bin/git for every other invocation (git 2.43.0 answers every other call): CONTROL, real git: `pool destroy --task t-old` exit 1, stderr `tiphys pool: cannot delete branch task/t-old: it is checked out at <tmp>/foreign; remove that worktree first`, branch present afterwards, foreign worktree still on refs/heads/task/t-old. WRAPPER: exit 0, stdout `destroyed t-old (deleted branch task/t-old was 22ece023b041cff38484cb7d0d4c123f5d4fd644)`, stderr EMPTY, `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/task/t-old` exit 1 afterwards, and the foreign worktree's status reads `## No commits yet on task/t-old`, the dangling HEAD the code comment names.

This is a regression of fix round 3, not a pre-existing gap of the same size: before 25dcb79 the listing was `worktree list --porcelain` without `-z`, which every git accepts, so the refusal fired on every git for every foreign worktree except the newline-path case round 3 set out to fix. After it, on a git without the option the refusal fires for NO foreign worktree, silently. What IS pre-existing is the shape that makes the regression silent: a nonzero listing exit is treated as `no foreign worktree` rather than as indeterminate, unlike the branch-tip read four lines above it (src/pool.ts:1119 `indeterminate`, refused at src/pool.ts:1187).

Not caught by the round's own witness: the named test test/pool.test.ts:431 and the spec witness/pool-destroy-newline-worktree-path.json exercise git 2.43 only, and the test's replay helper (test/pool.test.ts:405) runs the `-z` listing itself, so under the wrapper the test errors at the helper (`git worktree list --porcelain -z: error: unknown switch 'z'`) before destroy runs; the fixture above is what shows destroy's behaviour. The other six `-z` additions of rounds 2 and 3 (`diff -z`, `diff --cached -z`, `ls-tree -z`) are options every git accepts and are not in this finding.
findings.concrete-fix: Two parts, both small. (1) Fail closed at src/pool.ts:1130: when `worktree list` exits nonzero, refuse the destroy with the listing's stderr (`cannot determine which worktrees hold branch <name>: <stderr>; refusing to finish destroy`), the way the indeterminate branch tip is refused, so a listing failure of ANY cause is a refusal and never a proceed; red-witness it with a `git` stub on PATH that fails the listing (the pattern test/pool.test.ts:179 already uses for fetch) and assert exit nonzero, the branch present and the foreign worktree still on the branch. (2) Either declare and check a git floor in doctor (>= 2.36 if `-z` stays), or read the listing in the form every git prints (`--porcelain` without `-z`, splitting records on the blank line and paths on the first newline is not enough, since the path can hold one, so prefer the floor). Medium rather than high because it needs a git older than 2.36 on the machine running destroy; medium rather than low because on such a machine a destructive command loses a guard the kernel's own comment says only this code enforces, with nothing printed, and the fix round that introduced it was the one meant to harden that guard.
findings.analysis: Hazard class: what can destroy. The T-008 shape one level down: a guard whose precondition (a git option) is not tested is green and worthless on the toolchain where the precondition fails, and it fails without a word. The wrapper isolates the flag rather than the version, so the measurement is of the mechanism (a rejected option makes the listing exit nonzero, which the code reads as no foreign worktree) and would hold for any other cause of a nonzero exit.

evidence: New in this delta. src/witness/run.ts:246 newSidePathOfHeader decodes a C-quoted `+++` header only when the line ENDS with a double quote, and drops a trailing TAB only from an UNQUOTED header. git appends the TAB whenever the label contains a space, including a quoted label (diff.c tests the quoted string), so a name with a space AND a byte that forces quoting gets `+++ "b/src/caf\303\251 x.ts"<TAB>`, which neither branch recognises. Measured on git 2.43.0: `git diff -U0 --no-renames base...head | grep '^+++' | cat -A` prints `+++ "b/src/caf\303\251 x.ts"^I$`.

Consequence, measured through the exported function at ea3edb3 (`import('src/witness/run.ts')`, computePhaseDiff over a scratch repository with `src/plain.ts` (6 lines, line 1 changed) and `src/zcaf<U+00E9> x.ts` (8 lines, line 8 changed)): `{"path":"src/plain.ts","status":"M","hunks":[[1,1],[8,8]]}` and `{"path":"src/zcaf<U+00E9> x.ts","status":"M","hunks":[]}`. The quoted file's hunk is credited to the file whose header came before it, because an unrecognised `+++` line leaves `current` (src/witness/run.ts:365-369) pointing at the previous file. plain.ts has no line 8.

Two effects, both narrow. For the quoted file, rule (d) (src/witness/run.ts:1421-1437) can never find a mutation inside a changed hunk, so any witness over it is refused: red, fail closed. For the preceding file, rule (d) can be satisfied by line ranges that belong to another file: fail open, but only for a witness mutating the alphabetically preceding changed file at lines that coincide with the quoted file's hunks. The listing side (src/witness/run.ts:343, `-z`) is correct, so coverage still demands a witness for the quoted file. The round's decorated-names test (test/witness.test.ts:2705) drives a space and a non-ASCII byte in separate names, never both in one; the fall-through predates round 3 (the old regex did not match any quoted header either), and round 3 narrowed it.
findings.concrete-fix: In newSidePathOfHeader strip one trailing TAB before testing for the closing quote (git adds the TAB after the quoted label), and on any `+++ ` line that is recognised as neither a decodable header nor `/dev/null`, set `current = undefined` so orphan hunks are attributed to no file rather than the previous one; add `src/caf<U+00E9> x.ts` (space plus a quoting byte) to the decorated-names test and assert its hunk lands on it and on nothing else. Low: the misattribution needs a rare name shape and an adjacent file, and the direct effect on the quoted file is a red.
